column1: # BATCH 17 — pitch layout most=G high=G mid=E low=G least=E
# Elevated slots are mid and least. LEAST TAKES LANE B — least is the inverse fully
# embraced in all five, which is a withdrawal or a slackening, and jeopardy deflates
# those. MID takes either lane.
# The axis work below was done separately, against the three source files for each
# entry and against every neighbouring trait already written. THE POLES ARE FIXED.
# Steps 2-8 are to be worked on top of this; do not re-derive the axes, and do not
# quietly widen a pole to fit a scene you like. If a scenario will not sit on the pole
# as written, the scenario is wrong.
# Rows are still to be added at step 4. Run `plan` before any prose exists.
# === bitter-fermented-navy — bookish / cloistered / unread
# AXIS: reading is where you actually live — the book is the company, the day is built
#   round it, and it has been that way long enough to be a structure rather than a
#   pastime. Navy believes in structures; bitter is the acquired taste that will not
#   yield to the impatient; fermented is the work done privately, out of sight, and not
#   offered up for discussion.
# NOT: scholarly (bitter-fermented-cannellini, batch 08 — SAME FLAVOUR AND SAME FORM,
#   the sharpest trap in this batch). Scholarly is KNOWLEDGE DEPLOYED: its five facets
#   are a mistranslation caught at press night, a Polish grammar bought for a dying
#   grandmother, a book about damp brought to bear at a hardware counter, a Latin class,
#   a plaque contradicted. Every one of them turns on the reader being RIGHT about
#   something. Bookish never does. Nothing here may be settled by the reader knowing a
#   fact, and no facet may have the reader correct anybody.
#   NOT antiquarian (bitter-fermented-adzuki, batch 03 — the old object and its keeping;
#   this is about the reading, not the artefact). NOT studious — there is no
#   qualification anywhere in this entry, no exam, no course. NOT introverted: the
#   inverse is unread, not unsociable, which the LEAST pole has to respect.
# POLES, as bare dispositions:
#   MOST  cloistered — the book is chosen over a person who needed you, and the choosing
#         is not a slip. The room is available and you are not in it.
#   HIGH  bookish — a real cost is paid to keep the reading intact when something with a
#         proper claim on the hours turns up.
#   MID   bookish, low pitch — a small daily arrangement made in the reading's favour,
#         at some inconvenience nobody else would accept.
#   LOW   unread, low pitch — the book goes down for something, willingly and for a
#         stated reason, and is not picked back up.
#   LEAST unread — reading has no purchase on you at all, and there is no loss in it.
#         WATCH THIS ONE: it must be that the BOOK has no hold, not that the reader is
#         busy, sociable or outdoorsy. Those are a different axis and the pole collapses.
# === bitter-smoked-fava — otherworldly / unearthly / earthbound
# AXIS: the terms everyone else is running on — money, security, status, what people
#   will think — have no purchase on you, and you act on terms nobody in the room can
#   locate. Fava moves toward the difficult thing and starts before the outcome is
#   guaranteed, so this is ACTIVE, not dreamy; bitter is the palate that will not be
#   argued into the easy option; smoked means the source of it is never visible.
# NOT — and this entry has THREE written same-flavour-same-form neighbours, so the
#   separations matter more here than anywhere else in the batch:
#   eerie (bitter-smoked-green, approved) is the UNEASE THE READER CREATES IN OTHERS.
#   haunting (bitter-smoked-kidney, approved) is WHAT LINGERS with people afterwards.
#   oracular (bitter-smoked-adzuki, batch 04) is a MANNER OF SPEECH — pronouncements
#     where plain advice was wanted.
#   hermetic (bitter-smoked-cannellini, batch 09) is SEALEDNESS, being closed off.
#   So otherworldly is not an effect on other people and not a way of talking. It is
#   what the reader treats as mattering. NOTHING SUPERNATURAL, nothing spooky, no
#   religion, no atmosphere — the default failure on this word is a ghost story, and a
#   ghost story is eerie, which is already written and approved.
# DESIGN RULE, settled here so it does not have to be argued later: the reader's grounds
#   are never stated. Put the act on the page and leave the why off it, the way the
#   perception traits work. The moment a line explains the reasoning it becomes oracular,
#   or worse, merely eccentric. What makes it read is that the act is plainly costly and
#   plainly deliberate and no reason is given.
# POLES, as bare dispositions:
#   MOST  unearthly — you act on your own terms where somebody else carries the cost,
#         and you cannot be reached on theirs at all.
#   HIGH  otherworldly — a real and expensive choice made on grounds nobody present can
#         see the sense of, and you do not explain it.
#   MID   otherworldly, low pitch — something ordinary weighed on a scale nobody else is
#         using, in a moment small enough that it costs only you.
#   LOW   earthbound, low pitch — the practical consideration wins once, for a reason
#         that is stated.
#   LEAST earthbound — it is decided entirely on the money, or the security, or what
#         people will think, and that is plainly the right call.
# === sour-boiled-mung — impartial / detached / biased
# AXIS: when two people you are tied to are on opposite sides, you weigh it on what
#   actually happened rather than on which of them is yours. Mung tends the conditions
#   and is the one things get brought to; boiled is the steadiness that holds while it
#   is worked out; sour is the acid that cuts the question down to what is true.
#   IMPORTANT: this is a form of CARE, not of coldness. The reader is trusted, which is
#   why they are in the middle of it in the first place.
# NOT: precise (sour-boiled-cannellini, batch 02 — accuracy of statement), sincere
#   (sour-boiled-adzuki, batch 10 — meaning it), literal-minded (sour-boiled-navy,
#   batch 06 — taking the words at face value). All three are same flavour and same form.
#   ALSO NOT, and these are queued rather than written, so do not eat them: fair
#   (sour-roasted-kidney) and fair-minded (sour-boiled-chickpea) are about OUTCOMES and
#   SHARES; logical (sour-boiled-edamame) is about reasoning. Impartial is about
#   ALLEGIANCE, and the distinguishing feature is the tie.
# DESIGN RULE: every facet needs TWO SIDES and a stated reason the reader is tied to one
#   of them. Without the tie this is ordinary fairness and there is nothing to vote on —
#   Accept becomes "yes, I would be a reasonable person". That is the failure to watch.
# POLES, as bare dispositions:
#   MOST  detached — you decline to be on your own person's side at the moment they
#         needed you to be, and the not-taking is itself the wound.
#   HIGH  impartial — you find against your own, with the tie named and the cost real.
#   MID   impartial, low pitch — you decline to take the side you are expected to take,
#         in something small enough that nobody would have blamed you for taking it.
#   LOW   biased, low pitch — you tip it toward your own once, knowingly, for a stated
#         reason.
#   LEAST biased — you back your own openly, against what actually happened, and you are
#         not troubled by it.
# === spicy-dried-butter — taut / brittle / slack
# AXIS: everything is held at exactly the tension it needs and nothing is let go slack —
#   and the holding does not show, because the surface is calm. Butter lowers the
#   temperature of a room and cannot be hurried; spicy is what puts the whole thing under
#   load and makes it matter now; dried undergoes nothing, waits intact, and fractures
#   rather than yields. The bean is the interesting part: this is tension held inside the
#   one bean that is supposed to be soft, so none of it is visible from outside.
# NOT: tough (spicy-dried-navy, approved, and FACETS.md's own worked example of this
#   flavour and form) — tough is HEAT ABSORBED with no visible change, about what you
#   take. Taut is about what you HOLD, and holding is continuous where absorbing is an
#   event. NOT conductive (spicy-dried-chickpea, batch 15 — transmission, things passing
#   through). NOT firm (sour-dried-navy, batch 05 — a position that does not move under
#   pressure; that is one push, this is a rope kept tight for months). Queued siblings to
#   stay off: contained is holding something IN, primed is readiness to act.
# DESIGN RULE: the surface stays calm everywhere. There is no shouting in this entry
#   except at MOST, and even there the snap must be plainly disproportionate to the small
#   thing that caused it — that disproportion is what makes it brittle rather than angry,
#   and it is the only evidence the pole has.
# POLES, as bare dispositions:
#   MOST  brittle — the tension has been held past what it will take and it goes all at
#         once, over something far too small to explain it.
#   HIGH  taut — you hold the line at full tension when letting it down one notch would
#         be easy, reasonable, and unnoticed, and the holding costs you something named.
#   MID   taut, low pitch — a small standard kept tight where slack would never be
#         detected and nobody is asking for it.
#   LOW   slack, low pitch — you let one go, deliberately and for a stated reason.
#   LEAST slack — the whole thing is let loose and it is a relief. Not collapse, not
#         failure: a choice, with the price of it visible.
# === sweet-fried-black — ardent / feverish / tepid
# AXIS: a devotion that burns steadily for one person or one cause, commits you without
#   hesitation, and is never once said out loud. Sweet means it is FOR somebody rather
#   than for yourself; fried commits immediately and irreversibly, and the doing is the
#   thinking; Black gives nothing away about its interior, which is where the whole
#   difficulty of this entry lives.
# NOT: effusive (sweet-fried-pinto, batch 11 — SAME FLAVOUR AND SAME FORM). Every one of
#   effusive's five facets is the same move: the thing said out loud to somebody's face —
#   what she was like at nine, said to her new partner; said to a grandmother in a
#   hospice; said to the friend who drove three hours. ARDENT MAY NOT BE SAID.
#   NOT passionate (umami-fried-adzuki, batch 06). NOT doting (sweet-fried-kidney,
#   queued — indulgence of a person). NOT romantic (sweet-fried-navy, queued) — this need
#   not be love at all, and at least one facet should be for a cause rather than a person
#   so the entry does not read as a relationship entry.
# DESIGN RULE, and it is the whole entry: THE ACT IS NEVER A DECLARATION. It is what the
#   reader does, and keeps doing, at cost, without announcement. If a closing sentence
#   begins "You tell her…" or "You say…", the facet has been written for batch 11 and
#   must be rebuilt. The heat has to be inferable from the size of what is given up.
# POLES, as bare dispositions:
#   MOST  feverish — you commit something you cannot afford, past the point anybody
#         asked for or wanted, and the disproportion is the pole.
#   HIGH  ardent — a real and costly thing done quietly for the person or the cause,
#         unasked, and not mentioned to them or to anyone.
#   MID   ardent, low pitch — a small piece of devotion done without announcement, where
#         announcing it would have been the natural thing.
#   LOW   tepid, low pitch — the warmth is real and what you actually do about it is
#         mild, for a reason.
#   LEAST tepid — you feel perfectly warmly and it commits you to nothing whatsoever,
#         and that is a settled position rather than a failing.
# ============ STEP 2 — what is off-limits ============
# navy: fortunes own the silverfish in book spines, "read enough about it and the doing
#   never starts", "the book had the answer after all", "ask somebody who's done it",
#   "practice teaches what reading cannot", barley koji. OLD FACETS: a bindery and a
#   sewing frame with a wedding invitation in your coat; a mower manual fetched from the
#   house; a seed catalogue gone through with a pencil; a hedge-laying course turned up
#   to with empty hands; a self-taught man explaining when the glue has gone off.
#   QUESTION owns a niece who failed an exam and having a passage read to her. So NO
#   manuals, NO bookbinding, NO catalogues, NO courses, NO reading aloud to anybody.
#   NOTE the fortunes are all READING VERSUS DOING. That frame is spent — the axis here
#   is reading as company and structure, not reading as a substitute for competence.
# fava: fortunes own the selkie leaving its skin, "live far enough out and nobody can
#   reach the door", "the strange idea turns out to be the right one", "talk about the
#   weather for once", "ordinary company is a kind of rest", olive wood and wild thyme.
#   OLD FACETS: out at the stones since it got light; fog on a ridge; a dream kept a
#   fortnight; somebody's coincidence and asking what time their train is; a moon over
#   the estuary and the immersion heater. QUESTION owns a brother, a parking permit and
#   a roofer's invoice. So NO standing stones, NO fog, NO dreams, NO coincidences, NO
#   moons, NO household admin with a sibling.
# mung: fortunes own the crane standing still for either bank, "stay neutral long enough
#   and nobody notices the neutral one", "the even-handed read is worth having", "come
#   down on one side", "bias is what makes people useful to their friends", kokum.
#   OLD FACETS: two brothers fallen out over the business, given the same account each;
#   a footpath dispute chaired; a talent show judged with the mother three rows back; a
#   school place between two children; your own boy given not out. QUESTION owns two
#   flatmates coming separately about the same argument. The whole old set is FORMAL
#   ADJUDICATION — so no judging, no chairing, no umpiring, no panels anywhere. The
#   reader holds no office in this entry, which suits the axis better anyway: impartial
#   is about allegiance, not about a role.
# butter: fortunes own the whip snake, "anything held tight enough snaps at the smallest
#   thing", "small things stack up faster than big ones", "you can let this one slip",
#   "slack rope doesn't snap", numbing oil and drawn wire. OLD FACETS: an arrow at full
#   draw and a phone going off; a high wire; a lock gate shouldered shut; swimming to the
#   second buoy; seedlings not pricked out. QUESTION owns covering two jobs and a jammed
#   printer. The old set is almost entirely PHYSICAL TENSION as metaphor, so these five
#   go social and domestic instead — which the axis wants, because the surface has to
#   stay calm and a rope does not have a surface.
# black: fortunes own the cardinal, "say the warm thing first", "one warm sentence
#   changes a whole exchange", "steady beats blazing here", "mild enthusiasm lasts
#   longer", cinnamon sugar. OLD FACETS: six weeks of reading everything she recommended
#   and the route past her road; a subject found in October with three books and a trip
#   booked; telling them out loud what two years has meant; a band from when you were
#   nineteen let go; standing at the back with your coat while everyone else is up.
#   QUESTION owns swimming in the river before work. So NO new-crush research, NO
#   subject-plus-trip, NO gigs or bands, NO new exercise regimes. Note that three of the
#   five fortunes instruct the reader to SAY the warm thing — which is exactly what the
#   step 1 design rule forbids. The fortunes are off-limits and the rule stands.

# LANE B — how the tour runs and who runs it: the lamps, the cage down, the guide who worked the seam, the trust that shuts in a year without people.
# ============ COLD READ (on the final text, after all editing) ============
# Housekeeping first, so it survives the handover: a previous pass on this batch left 25
# of its own rows in this file above the STEP 2 block. They were removed before planning
# and none of them are in the ledger. Separately, `plan` had an edge case — once a
# batch's own rows fill the last thin bucket partway through its own validation, THIN
# comes back empty and the check then fails against an empty list. Guarded in
# facet-ledger.mjs: an empty THIN set means the requirement is vacuous.
# Fixed at the lint: one setting-carrying noun ("the shift"), three uses of regional
# slang, one stack of clauses before the main verb, and one closing act that was a
# not-doing wearing an active verb ("leave the shopping where it is" — which is the
# example in FACETS.md, so the linter was simply right).
# THE READ FOUND TEN. Seven were the usual thing: a noun in the act that the setup never
# bought — a hotel room, a paid-for trip, a supermarket belt, a watch, flowers, a bucket,
# a box. TWO WERE NOT REFERENT FAULTS AT ALL, and both were caught by the third list
# rather than the first two, which is the whole reason that list exists:
#   navy low  — the facet gave up "the hour you have had to yourself", never saying it
#               was the reading hour. Every referent was correct and the pole was gone:
#               it had become a facet about being busy, which is the exact collapse the
#               step 1 note warned about for this entry's inverse.
#   mung high — the other boy had no claim on the page, so finding against your own read
#               as arbitrary rather than impartial. Impartial means weighing on what
#               happened, so what happened has to be visible.
# All ten are RE-READ below on the new text and marked.
# bitter-fermented-navy
#  most  RE-READ. A do-not-disturb sign needs a room, and the page had only put the
#        family downstairs. Now "you are up in the room".
#        ON THE PAGE: the whole family are down in the bar; first time in four years they
#        have all been in one place; your uncle has come from Canada for it; you are up
#        in the room, three hundred pages into something you started on the train.
#        ACT NEEDS: the do-not-disturb; the door — the room is now stated.
#        POLE NEEDS: cloistered — the room is available and the claim on you is at its
#        maximum and named twice (four years, Canada). The book is not a refuge from
#        anything unpleasant, which is what keeps this the excess of bookish rather than
#        avoidance. RESIST: go down.
#  high  ON THE PAGE: the new rota gets you off at four instead of six; everybody else has
#        been after it for a year; what it takes away is the two hours in the canteen
#        before you start; that is where you have got through most of what you have read
#        in three years; the man doing the swaps has the sheet out.
#        ACT NEEDS: him; the late one = the six finish.
#        POLE NEEDS: bookish, and the cost is what makes it the high pole — "everybody
#        else has been after it for a year" is the clause that prices the hours. Note it
#        is reading AS A STRUCTURE, not reading instead of competence, which is the frame
#        the fortunes own. RESIST: take the four.
#  mid   ON THE PAGE: the tour has fifteen minutes left; the specimens are what everybody
#        has come for — the jars, the wax models, the skeleton of a man who sold it
#        himself; off the gallery a reading room where the surgeons' casebooks are kept;
#        a woman on the desk who will get one down if you ask.
#        ACT NEEDS: the fifteen minutes; in there = the reading room.
#        POLE NEEDS: bookish at low pitch — the written thing chosen over the thing
#        everyone came for, at a small stated cost. Nobody is corrected about anything,
#        which is the guard against scholarly. RESIST: go and see the specimens.
#  low   RE-READ, AND THIS WAS A POLE FAULT. The line gave up "the hour you have had to
#        yourself since you moved" — true, but it never said what the hour was for, so
#        the facet was about being busy and the axis had gone. Now "the hour you read in
#        and the only one you get".
#        ON THE PAGE: you cannot swim properly; the adult lessons are Wednesdays at
#        seven; that is the hour you read in and the only one you get; six weeks of them;
#        no other time that runs. ACT NEEDS: your name; the lessons.
#        POLE NEEDS: unread at low pitch, and it must be the BOOK losing its hold rather
#        than the reader becoming sociable — which is why the hour has to be named as the
#        reading hour on the page. RESIST: keep the hour.
#  least ON THE PAGE: your friend has taken you into the store where the pictures that
#        are not up live on racks you pull out; she has told you how a wall gets chosen
#        and what the conservator does to a frame first; at the end she gives you the
#        catalogue she wrote the essay in.
#        ACT NEEDS: her; the rest = the rest of what she was telling you; the way out.
#        POLE NEEDS: the inverse fully, and it is precise about which inverse — the book
#        is in your hand, written by somebody you like, and it has no purchase, while the
#        person does. Freedom (you get it live and better) and price (she wrote it and
#        you will not read it). RESIST: read the essay.
# bitter-smoked-fava
#  THE DESIGN CHECK, run on all five: no facet states the reader's grounds. The acts are
#  plainly costly and plainly deliberate and no reason is given anywhere, which is what
#  separates this from oracular (which explains, in pronouncements) and from eccentricity
#  (which has a reason and it is a silly one).
#  most  ON THE PAGE: the offer went in on Monday and was accepted on Tuesday; your
#        partner has given notice on her flat; the survey is booked for the morning;
#        there is nothing wrong with the house and nothing you could put into words.
#        ACT NEEDS: her; it = buying the house; the doorstep.
#        POLE NEEDS: unearthly — somebody else carries it (the notice is given, and that
#        is the cost stated) and you cannot be reached on the practical terms, which is
#        exactly what "nothing wrong with the house" establishes. Delete that clause and
#        the reader simply has cold feet. RESIST: go through with it.
#  high  ON THE PAGE: your gran left you and your brother twenty-two thousand each; his
#        has gone on a deposit for a flat; a trust that keeps a seabird colony on an
#        island you have never been to and could not point to; the woman at the counter
#        asks twice whether you want to sleep on it.
#        ACT NEEDS: the whole twenty-two.
#        POLE NEEDS: otherworldly — the brother's deposit is the visible sensible
#        alternative, and the island is deliberately given no connection to the reader,
#        because a connection would be a reason and the design rule forbids one.
#        RESIST: put it on a deposit like his.
#  mid   ON THE PAGE: down in the last chamber the guide puts the lights out for thirty
#        seconds so everybody can feel what dark is; there is the usual laughing; a child
#        asks him to put them back on; he has the switch in his hand and the tour behind
#        him. ACT NEEDS: him; them = the lights.
#        POLE NEEDS: otherworldly at low pitch — everybody else's scale is on the page
#        (the laughing, the child) and yours is plainly a different one, and it costs only
#        you. RESIST: laugh with the rest of them.
#  low   ON THE PAGE: you had decided to give the flat up and go with nothing arranged
#        past the first month; the housing officer goes through what that means — the
#        tenancy gone, and the list at nine years if you ever want back on it.
#        ACT NEEDS: another year.
#        POLE NEEDS: earthbound at LOW pitch — the practical wins once and the reason is
#        stated and specific (nine years), which holds it short of the inverse.
#        RESIST: give it up and go.
#  least RE-READ. "You take the refund" needed money paid, and two years of planning is
#        not paying. Now "and have all paid".
#        ON THE PAGE: the eleven of you have been planning it two years and have all paid;
#        the briefing is the insurance, what a helicopter off the mountain costs, and what
#        happens to the group if the weather turns on the third day; nobody else has
#        moved. ACT NEEDS: the refund.
#        POLE NEEDS: the inverse fully — decided entirely on the money and the risk, and
#        plainly the right call, with "nobody else has moved" making it a choice rather
#        than the room's consensus. Freedom (you are not on a mountain in bad weather)
#        and price (two years, and ten people). RESIST: go anyway.
# sour-boiled-mung
#  THE TIE CHECK, run on all five: every facet has two sides and states why one of them
#  is the reader's. Without that this entry is a person being reasonable, and Accept
#  becomes "yes, I am a fair-minded sort", which is not a vote.
#  most  ON THE PAGE: your sister and her partner have split; both of them have been at
#        yours since; she has asked you outright to say he was in the wrong about the
#        money. ACT NEEDS: her; he; Christmas.
#        POLE NEEDS: detached rather than impartial — she asked OUTRIGHT, which means a
#        side was owed and named, and the answer is not a judgement but a hospitality
#        arrangement, which is the refusal to be hers. That is the wound.
#        RESIST: say he was in the wrong.
#  high  RE-READ, AND THIS WAS A POLE FAULT. The other boy had no claim on the page, so
#        putting his name down read as arbitrary, or as an aversion to favouritism —
#        neither of which is impartial, which means weighing what actually happened. Now
#        "The other one has been every week since September".
#        ON THE PAGE: you do Tuesdays at the youth club; one paid place on the
#        residential; two of them want it; the other one has been every week since
#        September; yours is your neighbour's son, known since he was born, whose mum got
#        you the volunteering. ACT NEEDS: the other one's name; the place.
#        POLE NEEDS: impartial — a claim on the merits for the one you owe nothing, and a
#        tie stated twice for the one you do. Both halves are needed and neither carries
#        it alone. RESIST: put his name down.
#  mid   ON THE PAGE: you have brought your friend in with her wrist; the nurse is working
#        out who goes first, not by the clock but by what is wrong with them; your friend
#        wants you to say the pair of you have been here since half nine, which is an hour
#        out. ACT NEEDS: the nurse; what time you actually came in.
#        POLE NEEDS: impartial at low pitch — the tie is stated (you brought her), the ask
#        is explicit, and the cost is small enough to keep it off the high pole.
#        RESIST: say half nine.
#  low   ON THE PAGE: a woman with a pram asks which of the two bread stalls to go to;
#        your neighbour has the smaller one; it is her first year; it is not the better
#        bread. ACT NEEDS: her = the woman; your neighbour's.
#        POLE NEEDS: biased at low pitch — both the tie and the truth are on the page, so
#        the tip is knowing rather than ignorant, and it is small and has a stated reason.
#        RESIST: send her to the better one.
#  least ON THE PAGE: you have come in with your friend about his landlord; the adviser
#        has forty minutes and a form that wants the whole history in order; she asks
#        whether the rent was paid on time throughout; it was not — he missed two months
#        in the spring, and you know because he borrowed it off you.
